full_judgment: 3. The defendants Nos. 2-5, 7 and 8 appeared in the suit and filed 2 separate sets of written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint and also raising the issue of misjoinder of parties. The defendant No.5 also filed an application on 30.9.1999 under. Order 1 Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure for striking out her name from the plaint contending, inter alia, that there was no cause of .action for filing the suit against her and that she was never a Director of the defendant No.1 and that she never mortgaged her house situated at Dhanmondi Residential Area in favour of the plaintiff bank by way of 2nd charge nor did. she execute any letter of guarantee and that if any such 2nd charge document or personal guarantee is produced that must be untrue and baseless and that she was out of the country from 8.9.1991 to 23.12.1991 and so there was no scope for her to execute 2nd charge or furnish personal guarantee on 12.11.1991 and that had she executed the 2nd charge documents the defendant No.1 would not have 'urged the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the defendant No.1 to do the documentation by letters dated 25.4.1993 and 21.5.1995: The learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) after hearing the parties by order dated 22.2.2000 allowed the above application and directed to strike out the name of the defendant No.5 from the plaint and also to delete from the plaint the properties of the defendant No.5 as described in schedule "H" of the plaint and also rejected the application filed by the plaintiff bank for attachment before' judgment. The plaintiff bank, being aggrieved, filed Writ Petition No. 1618 of 2000 and the High Court Divisions after hearing, relying on the decision reported yin 16 BLD (AD) 250. made the Ride absolute in part by setting aside the order of striking out the name' of the defendant No-5 from the plaint with the finding that the question as to whether the defendant No.5 had executed the charge document or not can be decided after evidence is taken at the trial and the High Court Division maintained the order of the trial court regarding of rejection of the application for attachment before judgment.
